title: India's exports jump 30% to $90 billion in October; trade deficit narrows to $20 billion
dek: Goods exports rose 45% from a weak October 2025, but the merchandise deficit is still close to $40 billion as oil and gold imports stay high.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
India's total exports of goods and services rose by nearly 30% to $89.99 billion in October 2026 from $69.27 billion a year earlier, according to data released by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Friday. Total imports rose more slowly, to $110.07 billion from $94.42 billion, so the overall trade deficit narrowed to $20.09 billion from $25.15 billion.

Merchandise exports were the main driver, climbing 45.06% to $49.47 billion from $34.11 billion. Merchandise imports rose to $89.35 billion from $76.69 billion. That leaves a goods-only deficit of about $39.9 billion for the month (our calculation from the ministry's figures), offset in part by a surplus on services.

## Services and the year so far

Services exports are estimated at $40.51 billion, up from $35.17 billion. The October services numbers are the ministry's estimates, because Reserve Bank of India data on services trade is available only up to September; they will be revised.

For April to October 2026, total exports were about $568.84 billion, up about 16.66% on the same period last year, the ministry said.

## Why the jump

The 45% rise in goods exports flatters the picture: October 2025 was a weak month, after the US imposed tariffs of up to 50% on many Indian goods in August 2025. The ministry's release did not break down the October growth by product or destination in the material The Declaration could read; that detail will be needed to judge how much of the gain came from the US market, from electronics and from higher-priced petroleum products.

On the import side, crude oil prices have stayed high because of the US-Iran war. Brent crude settled at $95.84 a barrel on Friday, according to reports. Expensive oil raises India's import bill and widens the goods deficit.

## Trade talks with the US

The figures come as India and the US try to close the first phase of a trade agreement covering goods. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Friday: "India-US trade talks are on the right track... We look forward to a successful conclusion soon." According to reports, the US has assured India that it will face a lower tariff rate than its regional competitors; neither government has confirmed this. India's sixth round of trade talks with Canada is also under way in Delhi until 20 November.

## What happens next

Wholesale price inflation for October is due on Monday, 16 November, according to the commerce ministry. September's wholesale inflation was 11.39%, up from 9.92% in August. Retail inflation for October, released this week, was 6.09%, above the Reserve Bank's 6% upper limit.
